facts.fact: Carthage was founded in the ninth century BCE on the Gulf of Tunis, developed into a Mediterranean trading empire and was subsequently rebuilt by Rome.
facts.excerpt: Carthage was founded in the 9th century B.C. on the Gulf of Tunis. From the 6th century onwards, it developed into a great trading empire covering much of the Mediterranean and was home to a brilliant civilization.
facts.location: Public page main heritage description; manually read November 1, 2026

facts.fact: The archaeological property contains remains from several cultures and includes Byrsa, the Punic ports, Antonine baths and other components.
facts.excerpt: The property comprises the vestiges of Punic, Roman, Vandal, Paleochristian and Arab presence. The major known components of the site of Carthage are the acropolis of Byrsa, the Punic ports, the Punic tophet, the necropolises, theatre, amphitheatre, circus, residential area, basilicas, the Antonin baths, Malaga cisterns and the archaeological reserve.
